title: Daemon coordination authority adapter
description: Objective: provide the missing production consumer edge for @moe/coordination so typed session/terminal traffic is mediated by real identity, recipient, effect, and durable-store facts rather than test-supplied callbacks. Deliverable: a focused daemon adapter that constructs createCoordinationService/createDurableMailbox over SqliteEventStore, authenticates through committed core session authority, resolves registered recipients/effect-session bindings from durable daemon records, and exposes bounded send/read/ack operations. NOT in scope: MCP framing, free-form chat, remote shell, lifecycle commands, or canary tests. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/coordination/coordination-adapter.ts/.js, coordination-adapter.test.ts, plus apps/daemon/package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml only for the @moe/coordination workspace dependency. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/coordination test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: The adapter uses real SqliteEventStore and committed session/recipient/effect records; no caller can inject a positive auth, recipient, or terminal-binding answer.
Authenticated addressed REQUEST/RESPONSE/EVENT/CONTROL/HANDOFF messages sequence, replay, and acknowledge durably across adapter recreation, with exact receipt/digest identity.

Forged/expired session, missing capability, unknown recipient, stale cursor, mailbox pressure, and unbound terminal effect each assert the exact @moe/coordination reason code and layer and leave lifecycle authority unchanged.
Advisory text and CONTROL/HANDOFF envelopes can never call a command/lifecycle service; a before/after authoritative-store assertion proves non-mutation.
The @moe/coordination dependency is the only manifest change; coordination, daemon, and repo gates exit 0 with explicit-path attribution.
taskRails: TDD every behavior change; every refusal test pins the exact stable reason code and refusing layer, and generated sweeps assert a positive case count.
Use only public package roots across package boundaries; no deep imports, test-owned authority, mock-backed acceptance, or optimistic UNKNOWN upgrades.
Keep production files focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; stage and commit only explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description:
READ-ONLY. This is a COMPOSITION task: every piece exists and the work is wiring them without weakening any. Re-measure before naming symbols.

WHAT YOU MUST SUPPLY — packages/coordination/src/coordination-ports.ts defines `CoordinationDependencies` with exactly five members: `authenticate` (CoordinationAuthenticator), `mailbox` (DurableMailbox), `now` (() => number), `resolveEffectBinding` (CoordinationEffectBindingPort), `resolveRecipient` (CoordinationRecipientRegistry).

THE SEAM IS ALREADY CUT FOR TWO OF THEM:
- `resolveRecipient`: apps/daemon/src/coordination/recipient-registry.ts exports `RecipientRegistryService` whose `resolveRecipient` member is ALREADY TYPED `CoordinationRecipientRegistry`. It drops straight in. That registry (task-04e4367, DONE) exists precisely so this adapter never injects a caller-supplied recipient answer.
- `mailbox` and the service: `createDurableMailbox` (packages/coordination/src/index.ts:28) and `createCoordinationService` (:34) are root-published, and apps/daemon/package.json already declares "@moe/coordination": "workspace:*".

THE ACCEPTANCE RULE THAT GOVERNS ALL THREE PORTS, and it is easy to satisfy wrongly: coordination-ports.ts pins the accepted answers to exact key sets — BINDING_KEYS ["capabilities","ok","principalId","sessionId"], RECIPIENT_KEYS ["known","role"], EFFECT_KEYS ["bound","effectId","sessionId"] — and only a FROZEN, EXACT, POSITIVE answer becomes a binding. A thrown, partial, extra-keyed or mutable answer is indistinguishable from no answer at all. So a port that returns correct facts in the wrong shape grants nothing while passing every fact-only assertion.

AUTHENTICATE comes from the durable session authority: SessionAuthorityService exposes `authenticate` (session-authority-contracts.ts:212) and `readActiveSession` (:214). Read both and choose deliberately — DoD 1 forbids a caller-injected positive auth answer, so the adapter must derive it from committed records.

DoD 5 says "the @moe/coordination dependency is the only manifest change". Check whether it is already declared — it is at HEAD — in which case there may be NO manifest change at all. Say which in your evidence rather than editing to match the sentence.

Record the baseline for all four verification legs: `pnpm --filter @moe/coordination test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.

MEASURE THE ONE PIECE I COULD NOT CONFIRM, and treat the answer as a gate. `resolveEffectBinding` must answer from committed daemon records with the exact shape EFFECT_KEYS ["bound","effectId","sessionId"]. I grepped apps/daemon/src for an effect-session binding record source and found only the recipient-registry files — no dedicated effect-binding record surface.

Establish which is true: (a) an effect-session binding record source exists under apps/daemon and I missed it, (b) recipient-registry-records.ts already carries the effectId/sessionId pairing this needs, or (c) no durable source exists yet.

IF (c): STOP AND REPORT BLOCKED naming the missing record surface symbol by symbol. Do NOT satisfy `resolveEffectBinding` with a caller-supplied or constant answer — DoD 1 forbids a caller-injected terminal-binding answer outright, and DoD 3 requires an unbound terminal effect to refuse with an exact code. A stubbed port would pass the happy path and silently grant terminal authority, which is the exact defect this task exists to prevent. That is a legitimate outcome to report, not a reason to improvise.

If (a) or (b), name the exact module and record shape you will read, and carry on.

TDD RED. Create apps/daemon/src/coordination/coordination-adapter.test.ts over a REAL SqliteEventStore on a real temp path (mkdtemp under the OS temp root, never inside the repo, removed in an afterEach that runs on failure — this host is win32). DoD 1 requires real store and committed records; a fake store would prove the adapter agrees with the test's idea of persistence rather than the store's.

Create sessions and recipients ONLY through the production writers (the session authority and the recipient registry), never by hand-crafting rows.

DoD 3 refusal cases, each pinning the exact @moe/coordination reason code AND the refusing layer, and each asserting lifecycle authority is UNCHANGED: forged session, expired session, missing capability, unknown recipient, stale cursor, mailbox pressure, and unbound terminal effect. Seven distinct cases; assert a generated sweep produced a NON-ZERO count.

DoD 2's durability clause is the one most likely to be skipped: sequence, replay and acknowledge ACROSS ADAPTER RECREATION. Close the adapter, rebuild it and the store from the same path, and assert the receipt/digest identity is byte-identical and the cursor resumes. Assert digests by exact equality, never by presence.

DoD 4 is a distinct property, not a variant of DoD 3: advisory text and CONTROL/HANDOFF envelopes can NEVER call a command or lifecycle service. Prove it with a BEFORE/AFTER assertion on the authoritative store — capture its state, drive advisory and CONTROL/HANDOFF traffic, and assert the store is unchanged. "No error was raised" does not prove non-mutation.

GREEN: apps/daemon/src/coordination/coordination-adapter.ts plus its one-line LF `.js` bridge (every module in this directory has one — match a sibling byte-for-byte in form).

Construct `createCoordinationService` and `createDurableMailbox` over the real SqliteEventStore and supply all five CoordinationDependencies from committed daemon facts: `authenticate` derived from the session authority, `resolveRecipient` wired directly to RecipientRegistryService.resolveRecipient (it already has the right type), `resolveEffectBinding` from whatever step 2 established, `mailbox`, and `now`.

EVERY PORT ANSWER MUST BE FROZEN AND EXACTLY KEYED per the acceptance rule in step 1. Return Object.freeze'd records with exactly BINDING_KEYS / RECIPIENT_KEYS / EFFECT_KEYS respectively — an extra field silently voids the binding. Never let a port throw; a thrown answer is treated as no answer, so convert failures into the typed negative the contract expects.

NO CALLER-INJECTED POSITIVES (DoD 1): the adapter takes a store and configuration, not pre-answered auth/recipient/effect verdicts. If a signature would let a caller pass a positive answer in, that is the defect this task exists to remove.

PUBLIC ROOTS ONLY across package boundaries (taskRail 2): import from "@moe/coordination", never a deep path into packages/coordination/src. Within apps/daemon, relative imports are correct and expected.

Expose bounded send/read/ack only. NOT in scope: MCP framing, free-form chat, remote shell, lifecycle commands, canary tests. Target <=250 physical lines by `grep -c ''`, split before 400.

Mutation drills, then restore byte-exact. Each must redden a NAMED test; record the exact failing assertion. (a) Return the recipient answer UNFROZEN, or with one extra key — a test must redden; if none does, your tests assert the facts without asserting the shape the contract actually accepts, and the binding would silently never form. (b) Accept a caller-supplied positive auth answer — the forged-session case must redden. (c) Let `resolveEffectBinding` answer positively for an unbound effect — the unbound-terminal-effect case must redden. (d) Let a CONTROL or HANDOFF envelope reach a command service — the before/after store assertion must redden; if it stays green, that test is only checking for an absent error. (e) Break cursor persistence so replay restarts — the across-recreation digest equality must redden. (f) Change only the refusing LAYER on one refusal — a layer assertion must redden independently of the code.

The new files are UNTRACKED, so `git diff` is blind to them — hash with `git hash-object` before and after rather than trusting an empty diff, and re-run the suite after every restore.

Verify and self-review. (1) Run all four legs the task names, fresh and last: `pnpm --filter @moe/coordination test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck`. The coordination leg matters because this adapter is that package's first production consumer — if its own suite reddens, the composition is wrong, not the suite. (2) taskRail 2 check: `grep -rn "packages/coordination/src" apps/daemon/src/coordination/` must return NOTHING — public roots only, no deep imports. Paste the empty result. (3) Hand-measure the new production file with `grep -c ''` against the 250 target. (4) DoD 5: state whether any manifest change was needed at all; @moe/coordination is already declared at HEAD, so "the only manifest change" may be zero changes. Do not edit the manifest to match the sentence. (5) Path-attributed baseline repo-wide; intersect the failing-path delta with owned paths; confirm EMPTY. NOTE `pnpm test:fault` is currently red at j4 for an unrelated over-broad probe (task-bb7876d5 owns it) — disclose, do not chase. (6) Adversarial review: can any caller inject a positive auth, recipient or terminal-binding answer? Is every port answer frozen and exactly keyed? Does any port throw rather than return a typed negative? Can advisory text or a CONTROL/HANDOFF envelope reach a command or lifecycle service? Does replay survive adapter recreation with byte-identical digests? Did I add lifecycle, MCP framing or chat surface? (7) Record that this closes the Clause 1 consumer edge for @moe/coordination, and that task-5e43a9e2 names this task among its five hard dependencies. (8) Commit by explicit pathspec over owned paths only.

comments.author: architect-8c9073cd
comments.content: Fresh committed-byte audit at HEAD 7183c045 disproves the reopened-task premise. SqliteEventStore can back createDurableMailbox, but daemon has no production session/proof/replay authority, no recipient registry, and no effect-session resolver. @moe/core.authenticateCommand cannot authenticate coordination endpoints: it requires RuntimeCommandEnvelope/RuntimeCommandKind, while coordination uses SEND/READ/REPLAY/ACK plus colon-delimited capability strings that core CapabilityGrant cannot represent. Created prerequisites task-b4f12e63baca4ecc9f2c159ed3c3ad78 (reusable core session auth), task-21713cf152c047c597da9765d8d95510 (durable daemon session authority; proof protocol choice required), and task-04e4367443214a588ed6277b92969a33 (recipient registry); linked existing task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 for effect/session binding. Separate acceptance conflict needs human/governor correction: @moe/coordination deliberately returns typed CURSOR_GAP with durableCursor/mailboxSequence and has no cursor reason code/layer; historical behind-ack cursors are valid replay. Amend DoD 3 to assert the exact CURSOR_GAP fields, or explicitly authorize a coordination contract task—never invent adapter-local refusal vocabulary.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
STUBBING resolveEffectBinding IF NO RECORD SOURCE EXISTS — REJECTED, and step 2 makes it a hard gate rather than a judgement call. DoD 1 forbids a caller-injected terminal-binding answer and DoD 3 requires an unbound terminal effect to refuse with an exact code. A stubbed positive would pass the happy path while silently granting terminal authority — precisely the defect this adapter exists to remove. If no durable source exists, reporting blocked with the gap named symbol by symbol is the correct outcome.

A FAKE OR IN-MEMORY STORE IN TESTS — REJECTED by DoD 1, which requires real SqliteEventStore and committed records. A fake proves the adapter agrees with the test's model of persistence rather than the store's, and it cannot exercise DoD 2's across-recreation replay at all.

HAND-CRAFTING SESSION OR RECIPIENT ROWS — REJECTED. Create them through the production writers; the registry exists precisely so recipient answers come from committed records.

WIRING resolveRecipient THROUGH AN ADAPTER SHIM — UNNECESSARY. RecipientRegistryService.resolveRecipient is already typed CoordinationRecipientRegistry, so it composes directly. A shim would add a place for the frozen-exact shape to be lost in translation.

EDITING THE MANIFEST TO SATISFY DoD 5 — REJECTED. The DoD says the @moe/coordination dependency is the only manifest change, but it is ALREADY declared at HEAD. The honest reading is that zero manifest changes may be required; step 6 asks the worker to state which rather than making an edit to match the sentence.

planningNotes.risks:
1. A PORT THAT RETURNS CORRECT FACTS IN THE WRONG SHAPE. The contract accepts only a frozen, exact, positively-keyed record; anything else is silently treated as no answer. The adapter would look right, every fact-only test would pass, and no binding would ever form. Drill (a) targets it and it is the highest-probability defect here.

2. A STUBBED resolveEffectBinding. If the durable record source does not exist, the tempting fix is a constant or caller-supplied answer — which grants terminal authority silently and defeats DoD 1 and DoD 3 together. Step 2 makes blocking the required outcome instead.

3. CALLER-INJECTED POSITIVES GENERALLY. This task exists because the coordination service was previously driven by test-supplied callbacks. Any signature that lets a caller pass in a positive auth, recipient or effect verdict reintroduces exactly that.

4. DoD 4 TESTED AS ABSENCE OF AN ERROR. "Advisory text cannot call a command service" is only proven by a before/after assertion on the authoritative store. A test that checks no exception was thrown passes against an adapter that mutated state successfully.

5. DURABILITY TESTED WITHIN ONE PROCESS. DoD 2 requires sequence/replay/ack ACROSS adapter recreation with exact receipt/digest identity. An in-process reuse proves nothing about the cursor surviving.

6. DEEP IMPORTS. taskRail 2 requires public package roots only; a deep import into packages/coordination/src would work locally and violate the boundary. Step 6 asserts the absence.

7. IN-REPO SQLITE ARTEFACTS on a win32 host — mkdtemp under the OS temp root, cleaned on failure paths too.

8. THE MANIFEST SENTENCE IN DoD 5 invites an edit that is already done; state the fact rather than making a redundant change.
